## Overview

Offline embedding refresh jobs are scheduled batch processes that regenerate vector embeddings for a corpus when either:
- The underlying embedding model changes (model upgrade, retraining, or strategy shift)
- Source documents update in bulk (corpus refresh, content migration, or data correction)

Rather than triggering on demand, these jobs typically run on a fixed cadence, re-embed the full or incremental document set, and swap the new vectors into the retrieval index atomically to avoid serving mixed-model results mid-transition.

## Core Operations

**Re-embedding Strategy:**
- Full re-embedding: regenerate vectors for the entire corpus
- Incremental re-embedding: regenerate only for newly added or modified documents

**Atomic Swap:**
- New vectors are staged separately before replacing the current index
- The swap happens atomically to prevent serving stale and fresh vectors simultaneously
- This consistency is critical for retrieval quality and to avoid unexpected ranking shifts

## Operational Concerns

**Embedding Model Versioning:**
- Each batch run should version the embedding model used
- Track which model generated each set of vectors to enable rollback and debugging

**Vector Drift Monitoring:**
- Monitor the distance/divergence between old and new vectors for the same documents
- Detect quality regressions before serving new embeddings to users
- Drift can indicate model degradation or corpus changes that need investigation

**Blue/Green Index Staging:**
- Stage the new index (green) in parallel with the current production index (blue)
- Run validation queries and quality metrics against the green index
- If quality regressions are detected, roll back by keeping the blue index active
- If validation passes, atomically switch traffic to green
